decisions.evidence: R4 maker: prototype saves from a bar, each bookmark a card with 'preview image, site icon, source, title, description, and address'; auto-fills from just the pasted MDN url. R4 client: 'card looks right... I only had to paste the address and it filled the rest in.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Save-by-url, auto-collection of title/description/favicon/preview, and readability-first card display all conform to the reference. Placeholder preview image is a prototype stand-in (real image confirmed at R44), not a design divergence.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker asked only 'whether the resulting saved item contains the right at-a-glance information' (display scope). R4 client extended beyond it: 'if the title or description that gets pulled in isn't quite right, I'll want to be able to fix it.' Delivered R5 inline editor.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Editing of auto-collected title/description was absent from the display-focused presentation; client surfaced the reference requirement (edit before/after saving). Anticipatory extend, delivered next round.

decisions.evidence: R5 maker asserted a boundary: 'the address, site icon, and preview image remain tied to the original page' and asked 'whether that boundary is right.' R5 client: 'I wouldn't want the address locked down completely... being able to correct the address should be possible too when I open a bookmark to edit it.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Maker presented an editing scope that excluded the url, which contradicts REF-BM-04 (edit url/title/description/tags/note). Client supplied the reference-conforming behaviour (url must be editable). The inline-vs-dialog part is a functionally equivalent UI choice, excluded.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker presented a single-sentence plain note and asked 'whether the result matches how you'd expect a personal note to work.' R7 client extended: 'I'd expect to be able to write a note with a bit of light formatting... bullets as bullets, bold as bold... rather than showing the raw symbols.' Delivered R8.
decisions.note: Prototype review. The presented note lacked markdown rendering, which REF-BM-23 requires; client surfaced the missing capability. R8 toolbar-vs-markup is a functionally equivalent UI choice, excluded.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker presented label assignment as removable clickable pills; R9 client: 'labels are short reusable names, I can remove them while editing, and they show as pills on the card' — assumptions match.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Assigning one or more tags conforms to the reference. The pills-vs-comma entry method is a functionally equivalent UI choice, excluded.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker's stated label-entry assumptions (reusable names, removable, pills) omitted autocomplete. R9 client: 'as I start typing a label, I'd like it to suggest ones I've already used... when I type "Re…", it should offer my existing "Reference"... That's the piece missing from what I see here.' Delivered R10.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Autocomplete-on-tag-entry (REF-BM-10) was absent from the presented reusable-label design; client surfaced it explicitly as missing.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker: clicking the Reference pill keeps you in the collection, shows all bookmarks with that label, swaps heading, updates count. R11 client: 'exactly how I want to pull up just show me my reference links.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Tag-filtering conforms. Client's 'easy way back out' (clear filter) and the R12 clear-filter A/B are not distinct reference items / functionally equivalent, excluded.

decisions.evidence: R13 maker: search covers titles, descriptions, notes and ignores capitalization; searching 'FLEXBOX' matched via the note. R13 client: 'it looks across the title, the description, and my own notes, and ignores capitalization.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Case-insensitive search conforms. Live-vs-submit is a functionally equivalent UI choice, excluded.

decisions.evidence: R13 maker scoped search to 'titles, page descriptions, and personal notes' — omitting url. R13 client: 'I'd also want the web address itself to be searchable... type that and find it... please fold the address into what search looks through as well.' Delivered R14 ('MOZILLA' matches developer.mozilla.org).
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-12 requires full-text over title, description, note AND url; the stated scope omitted url, and the client extended to include it.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker asked 'Does that complete the search behavior you have in mind?' R14 client: 'a quick way to search by label right in the search box — something like typing #reference to pull up everything with that label.' Delivered R15.
decisions.note: Prototype review. #tag search was missing from the asked-about (declared-complete) scope; client surfaced it. R15 exact-label-match assumption confirmed conforming.

decisions.evidence: R14 client: 'combine terms. Like flexbox and #css, grid or flexbox, css but not #reference — and group things in parentheses... rome (#article or #book). And if I actually want to search for the word "and"... put it in quotes... when I mix a label search and a text search together, both have to match.' Delivered/confirmed R16-R19, R21.
decisions.note: Prototype review. AND/OR/NOT, parenthesised grouping, quoted-operators-as-literals, and tag+text AND-combining were all missing from the asked-about scope; client surfaced the full REF-BM-15 semantics.

decisions.evidence: R14 client: 'when I put something in quotes, I'd expect it to match that exact phrase, in that order, rather than the words scattered around.' Delivered R20: '"modern JavaScript"' kept only the exact-order match.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Quoted exact-phrase matching was missing from the asked-about scope; client surfaced it.

decisions.evidence: R22 maker: mark for later, status independent of labels and visible on card. R22 client: 'it's its own separate thing from labels and it stays visible on the card.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Read-later marking conforms. Direct-toggle-vs-edit is a functionally equivalent UI choice, excluded.

decisions.evidence: R23 maker: action removes read-later status but never deletes; R25 marking CSS grid read dropped it from the pile, count to one, still in collection. R25 client: 'it's only leaving the to-read pile, not being deleted.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Mark-as-read conforms. The toggle-vs-'mark as read' wording is a functionally equivalent choice, excluded.

decisions.evidence: R24 maker: sidebar 'Read later' shows only the two marked bookmarks with heading/count. R24 client: 'exactly the separate to-read view I wanted.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Separate unread view conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: R26 maker offered recently-saved default plus title A-Z/Z-A and asked whether orderings cover expectations. R26 client added oldest-saved-first; R27 confirmed 'newest-first and oldest-first by date, plus title both directions... Sorting's covered.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Sort-by-key conforms; the presented set already satisfies REF-BM-22 and the added oldest-first direction is a refinement within the same item, not a distinct reference divergence. Dropdown-vs-buttons is a functionally equivalent UI choice, excluded.

decisions.evidence: R28 client flagged as still-open 'what should happen if I try to save a link I've already saved.' R29 maker offered A=focus/go-to-existing vs B=offer 'save another copy.' R29 client selected A and rejected B: 'offering save another copy is the one thing I don't want... please go with A, and drop the save another copy path... match on the actual destination address, and never quietly make a second copy.' R38 confirmed tracking-param/fragment normalization.
decisions.note: Specification gate + prototype review. Option B (allow a second copy) diverges from REF-BM-06 (converge to editing the existing item); client selected the conforming alternative and negated the divergent one. Client surfaced the requirement at R28 (pending) and dispositioned it at R29 — counted once.

decisions.evidence: R28 maker asked holistically 'do all of those behaviors still fit together... as a whole?' R28 client: 'there are still a few everyday things... like removing a bookmark I no longer want.' Delivered R30 with a confirm safeguard; R41 confirmed empty-collection state after last delete.
decisions.note: Specification gate. At a holistic completeness checkpoint the reviewed scope omitted delete (a core reference item); client surfaced it. The R30 confirm-vs-undo safeguard is a functionally equivalent choice, excluded.

decisions.evidence: R30 client: 'I'd expect there to also be a gentler option alongside delete, for setting something aside in a way I can undo later. Not asking you to build it this second.' R43: 'set aside without deleting... tuck a bookmark out of my main list but get it back later, kept separate from permanent delete.' R44 restated as next-round work while accepting the cycle.
decisions.note: Specification gate / implementation review. Client explicitly identifies archive (reversible, distinct from permanent delete = REF-BM-26/27) and accepts completing this cycle without it. Reveals the requirement without implementing it; not requesting alignment of the current deliverable.

decisions.evidence: R43 client: 'Doing something to several bookmarks at once, rather than one at a time.' Reaffirmed R44: 'doing things to several bookmarks at once... I'd like us to pick up in the next round.' Explicitly not holding up the approved scope.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Client names bulk multi-select actions (REF-BM-20; REF-BM-21 apply-to-filtered-whole is a related finer point, not separately expressed) and accepts the departure from the current scope.

decisions.evidence: R43 client: 'Getting my existing bookmarks in, and my collection back out, since I've got links elsewhere I'd want to bring over.' Reaffirmed R44 as next-round work while accepting the cycle.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Client identifies import ('in') and export ('out') of bookmarks (REF-BM-30/31) and accepts building without them now.

decisions.evidence: R43 client: 'A couple of small personal display preferences beyond sort, like text size.' R44: 'a text-size preference... things I'd like us to pick up in the next round.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Client names a display-related personal setting (font/text size = REF-BM-32) and accepts its exclusion from the current scope. (Default-sort persistence, noted at R42, was delivered.)

decisions.evidence: R31 maker (missing metadata) proposed saving with site-name/visual fallbacks + notice + editor, asking whether saving should instead stop. R31 client: 'Saving shouldn't stop... keep the link no matter what.' R32 (invalid 'my notes page') refused with no bookmark; client: 'a bookmark is only meaningful if it points at a real web link.'
decisions.note: Prototype/edge review. Save-with-fallbacks (never blocking a valid url) and refusing a non-url both conform to REF-BM-01 (url required); the offered 'stop saving' alternative would have diverged but the client confirmed the conforming behaviour.
